gloss: first-time customer; new customer; first visit

definitions.gloss: first-time customer; new customer; first visit to an establishment
definitions.explanation: A customer visiting a shop, restaurant, or establishment for the first time. Often used in traditional Japanese businesses where regular customers are valued.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}は{一見|いちげん}さんお{断|ことわ}りだ。
examples.english: This shop doesn't accept first-time customers.

examples.japanese: {一見|いちげん}の{客|きゃく}でも{歓迎|かんげい}してくれた。
examples.english: They welcomed me even though I was a first-time customer.

examples.japanese: {紹介|しょうかい}がないと{一見|いちげん}では{入|はい}れない{料亭|りょうてい}だ。
examples.english: It's a traditional restaurant that first-timers can't enter without an introduction.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
{一|いち} (one/first) + {見|げん} (seeing/meeting)

Literally "first meeting/seeing" - refers to the first time a customer visits.

KEY PHRASE:
「{一見|いちげん}さんお{断|ことわ}り」 is a famous expression meaning "first-time customers not accepted." Common at:
- Traditional {料亭|りょうてい} (high-end Japanese restaurants)
- Exclusive お{茶屋|ちゃや} (teahouses in Kyoto)
- Member-only establishments
- High-end バー (bars)

CULTURAL NOTE:
This practice exists to:
- Maintain quality of service
- Ensure customers understand etiquette
- Protect privacy of regular customers
- Preserve exclusive atmosphere

Typically, a referral from a regular customer ({常連|じょうれん}) is needed for first-time entry.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一見|いちげん}さん - first-time customer (polite)
- {一見|いちげん}の{客|きゃく} - first-time customer
- {一見|いちげん}お{断|ことわ}り - no first-timers

CONTRASTED WITH:
- {常連|じょうれん} - regular customer
- お{得意|とくい}さん - valued regular customer
- {馴染|なじ}み - familiar customer

NOTE ON READING:
Different from {一見|いっけん} (at first glance) which has different kanji reading and meaning.
